findings.reason: Confirmed, and reproduced end to end. I checked every element of the evidence myself rather than accept the report's. (1) RS-15's link[1] is VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB4 -> VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB3:general-BC, and its reason does begin 'ADD ONLY AFTER deleting general-BC -> VB4', ending 'This is an atomic replacement, not an additional edge in the unmodified graph.' The layer VB3:general-BC has action 'narrow' with suppliedBy ['...VB3:projectivized-properness', '...VB4']. (2) research/blueprint/restructure/RS-15.result.json and data/restructure/RS-15.result.json are byte-identical, SHA-256 7ead28fbb6636ace04c2cad7b3295c91206492024fe5585e41ca1cafdf61a582, the hash the finding gives. (3) Reading scripts/restructure.py confirms the mechanism: the layers loop writes stage['restructured'] with the narrowing and its suppliers before the links loop runs, and inside the links loop 'if reaches(target, source)' appends to record['skippedLinks'] and continues, with no rollback of the narrowing already written; nothing anywhere parses the deletion instruction out of a link's reason, which is only stored as evidence. (4) I ran apply_restructurings read-only against data/atlas.json, with RS-15 alone and with all 23 promoted proposals, and got the same result both times: links 5, skippedLinks [['VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB4', 'VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB3:general-BC']], VB3:general-BC carrying restructured action 'narrow' with VB4 among its suppliers, the old edge general-BC -> VB4 still present and the new edge VB4 -> general-BC absent. (5) The live atlas extract agrees: general-BC -> VB4 is present as a stage edge and mirrored in VB4's requires and general-BC's consumers, while VB4 -> general-BC appears in none of the three, and VB3:projectivized-properness -> VB4 is retained. So the narrowing is in force while the precondition it was accepted on is not, which is exactly the claim. (6) The mathematical justification holds at its locator. I fetched the Fargues-Scholze Geometrization PDF from https://people.mpim-bonn.mpg.de/scholze/Geometrization.pdf on 24 September 2026 (SHA-256 begins 9ab9efbd, 357 pages) and the quoted sentence 'By Theorem II.2.19, the same is true in an open neighborhood, finishing the proof.' is on PDF page 76, whose first line is the printed number 76, so printed p.76 as cited; its context is the end of a proof in II.3 invoking the relative Harder-Narasimhan result II.2.19. That supports the direction of the required edge, VB4 supplying general-BC, and so supports repair by reversal rather than by deleting the edge to satisfy the guard. (7) The count in the fix's regression list checks out: VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals has 10 stages and BunGAndNewtonStrata 7, the seventeen it names. Medium severity is right: the finding does not claim a cycle, and there is none, but it changes what gets built, since a layer is narrowed to what it keeps while the supplier edge that was to replace the removed dependency is silently dropped. The fix is right as written, including its refusal to invent a JSON deletion key and its instruction to defer the narrowing until the replacement is executable. One addition I would make: the cheapest guard against recurrence is in the tool rather than in this proposal, since apply_restructurings applies a proposal's layer actions before its links and cannot undo them, a proposal whose links were skipped should not have its narrowings applied at all, and the run should fail loudly rather than record skippedLinks and continue. That belongs in the fix job, not here; as the finding says, the two-file red-team scope does not authorize the integration edits.
